results.content:
The need for a protocol purpose-built for AI agents has always bugged me. Great to see progress toward a standard that makes existing software constructs understandable to agents and reduces duplicate work. Some thoughts on the concerns you have raised: ▪️ MCP can be a quick solution for API owners to expose their APIs to agents, but the end goal should be APIs that agents can natively understand, with rich metadata, clear payloads, and well-structured endpoints. ▪️ With proper delegation, agents can act on a user’s behalf with scoped permissions. There are already a set of IETF drafts that aligns with this approach. ▪️ Multi-API calls should be handled by the agent itself through proper adapters, IMO.   To people wrapping the entire world with MCP: if a tool already has a good, self-documented command-line interface, you probably DON'T need to turn it into an MCP server. If the CLI of a tool makes it difficult for an agent to use it, please do not write an MCP interface to make it smoother for AI agents. Write a \better\ command-line interface to make it smoother for AI agents \and\ humans \and\ scripts.
